raw_recipe.headline: Taco Seasoning (without the chili powder)
raw_recipe.description: The title says it all. If you seek a recipe for taco seasoning that does not use chili powder, you've found it!
raw_recipe.name: Taco Seasoning (without the chili powder)

recipeInstructions.text: Combine all ingredients in a sealable container; store in a cool dry place.

review.reviewBody: This is really good, except I omitted the salt. One huge advantage of making my own seasoning mixture is that I can control the sodium. In this case, I add the necessary salt to taste in each individual dish. If the dish contains salty ingredients like tomato sauce or cheese, often no additional salt is necessary.

This was fabulous and my entire family loved it!
I didn't have red pepper flakes so I used 1/8 tsp. of cayenne instead.
I used 1/4 cup of seasoning to 1 lb. of ground turkey with 3/4 cup of water.
There was a decent kick to it and any spicier may have been too much for my kids (but not my husband and I).
While the meat was browning I added 1 Tbsp. of minced garlic. After the meat was browned, I drained it and added 3/4 Cup diced onion and 1 small diced green pepper (I sauteed the green pepper and onion separately before adding to the meat). I then added the seasoning and combined thoroughly before adding 3/4 Cup of water. I simmered uncovered for 15-20 minutes.
I will certainly be making this again!

This was great! I was looking for something more authentic and not containing a thickening agent like starch in store bought seasonings. I used some Spanish smoked paprika and it added a great Smokey flavor. I use about 1.5 - 2 Tbsp per pound of meat (ground turkey, shredded beef, pork or chicken) then simmer with water for a while then reduce it. I had my 9 year old prepare a large batch and store it in with the other spices.

Oh yeah! My family liked this as much as the packets, and this was fun to mix up. Of course I have to tweak everything. I reduced the salt and cayenne, added 2 tsp flour and 1 tsp beef bullion granules. Also added 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp allspice, 1/2 tsp ground thyme, 1/2 tsp ground marjoram, and 2 tsp ground coriander. Those are spices I use for my chili, so figured what the heck. Add 3/4 cup water and 2 Tbsp of spice mix to a pound of ground beef and cook down. Lovely! Thank you for the great recipe.
I added two teaspoons of corn starch to bind the hamburger meat and get the same consistency that the packaged seasoning seems to give. I also ran the seasonings through a blender.

I have a family member that doesn't tolerate even a small amount of cayenne, black pepper, or chilies. Omitting the black pepper and crushed red pepper flakes from this recipe still makes for a flavourful taco seasoning, so we can both enjoy the same meal. Today, I tried omitting the salt and replacing it with a teaspoon of Oxo beef bouillon powder for something different. The bouillon powder is pretty salty, so nixing the salt seemed to be a good plan. I was really pleased with the flavour.

Flavor is great but a bit too salty. I'll use 1 tsp salt next time. I also subbed 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper for the 1 tsp crushed red pepper and it's turned out a good "medium" heat. Very glad to find a recipe that doesn't use packaged chili powder.

My family loves the flavor of this taco seasoning. I am on a sodium restricted diet, so I reduce the salt to 1/2 teaspoon. And I add a tablespoon of flour and add water to the meat and seasoning to make it a little saucy. This is my go-to for taco night!

I was out of Old El Paso seasoning and so I tried this. It is excellent! I had to cut the red pepper flakes out because my family won’t eat any dish if they see pepper flakes. I added 1/2 tsp. of McCormick Cajun seasoning instead. Delicious...and my husband just gave me a smile and a thumbs up!
Thank you for sharing the recipe with us.

I really liked it. I used Ground Cayenne Red Pepper instead of the pepper flakes. I think it was spicier but that was a good thing. It says 10 servings but I used it all on 2 pounds of a ground beef/ground pork mixture and it was way more flavorful than I was expecting but so good. The family liked it.
I added a touch more garlic and also added .5 tsp of dried parsley. It's definitely a winner, I'll never buy the pre made stuff again!!!

Love using this for taco seasoning at home. I did make 1 tweak to the recipe. The red pepper flakes leave a spicy aftertaste, so I substituted “Tony Chachere’s Cajun Creole [original seasoning]” instead. Tastes a lot better.
Better then the store package

Thank you for this. It really needs to be the top hit for taco seasoning. It's frankly dumb that the more popular recipe contains chili powder, which is just a different blend of all the same stuff! I like to add a bit of cornstarch to this recipe - it kinda makes the meat come out a little saucier.
This mixture is really tasty!!!
Loved it! I can't eat chilli powder and this recipe is great.

I have been to the store several times and I keep forgetting chili powder. I made this with my daughter, I did not change any of the ingredients and she absolutely loved it and said it’s much better than the packet seasoning. We will be making it again today
I omit salt and adjust the heat to taste. We love the flavor.

Thank you, thank you, thank you for posting this! My taco meat tastes like tacos again! I've been looking for a taco seasoning recipe without salt, and like you say in the description most call for chili powder which is a mix of herbs that usually already has salt added in as well. So trying to find a no-salt chili powder recipe to turn in to taco seasoning, I ended up with something that had 10 TBS of paprika *facepalm*. Anyhow, this is so good, my tacos taste like tacos again HUZZAH

I’m not a fan of chili powder so this is perfect for me. I used smoked paprika & left out both peppers; threw in a sprinkle of onion salt then tossed it on cooked shredded chicken & put it in taco shells. Delish!
